added_after: independent reproduction, round 1: S3 (Ed448 public keys of small order) and S5 (evaluation order of inputs with more than one defect)

ed448_small_order.base: d2-vector-k1 of the V1 vectors: its descriptor with item 8 (Ed448 key) replaced, and its challenge with items 9 and 10 recomputed for that descriptor; the FN-DSA half is a fresh signature over the intent by the d2-vector-k1 FN-DSA key (fndsa_signatures)

forgery.construction: s = clamp(SHAKE256(seed, 114)[0..57]) reduced modulo the group order; R = encode([s]B) (the RFC 8032 public key of seed); S = s; signature = R || S. No private key of any small-order point is involved.

honest_control.name: honest d2-vector-k1 key with the forged Ed448 half

ed448_small_order.rule: An Ed448 public key (and R) must decode and must not be of order 1, 2 or 4 (refuse A when [4]A is the identity); the repository decodes through the 4-isogeny and refuses points it maps to the identity (build8_qual_ed448_public_valid). Under textbook RFC 8032 (section 5.2.3 decoding, section 5.2.7 check) the forgery below verifies under EVERY one of the four keys for every message, because [4]A is the identity (plain_rfc8032_ed448_verdict_of_the_forgery); the vendored OpenSSL verifier, like OpenSSL 3.5.7, already refuses the order-2 and identity encodings at decoding, so it accepts the forgery only under the two order-4 keys (vendored_openssl_ed448_verdict_of_the_forgery).

multi_defect_probes.name: class_phase_mismatch_and_truncated
multi_defect_probes.rule: D2 before D4: the truncated last item cannot be read, so the class/phase rule is never reached

multi_defect_probes.name: non_minimal_version_and_class_phase_mismatch
multi_defect_probes.rule: D2 reads a non-shortest integer by its value; D4 (class/phase) precedes D6 (re-encoding), which alone refuses the non-shortest form

multi_defect_probes.name: non_minimal_length_of_item_9
multi_defect_probes.rule: D2 reads a non-shortest length by its value; D6 (re-encoding) refuses it

multi_defect_probes.name: indefinite_length_profile
multi_defect_probes.rule: D2: every item has a definite length; an indefinite-length text string is not read

multi_defect_probes.name: invalid_utf8_in_the_profile
multi_defect_probes.rule: D2: item 8 must read as a valid UTF-8 text string; the profile comparison (V4) is never reached

multi_defect_probes.name: zero_nonce_and_trailing_byte
multi_defect_probes.rule: D3 (no byte after item 14) precedes D5 (zero fields)

multi_defect_probes.name: production_phase_with_an_ed448_only_signature
multi_defect_probes.rule: I2 (the 1,394-byte serialization) precedes every verification step, including the production refusal V1

multi_defect_probes.name: generation_two_descriptor_with_an_fndsa_only_signature
multi_defect_probes.rule: I2 precedes the descriptor checks V2 to V5

multi_defect_probes.name: descriptor_with_suite_2
multi_defect_probes.rule: V2: the descriptor decoder pins suite 1, policy 1 and the profile, before the challenge items are compared (V4)

multi_defect_probes.name: descriptor_ed448_key_not_a_point
multi_defect_probes.rule: V2: both public keys are validated when the descriptor is decoded

note: Public data only (TEST-VALUE keys from public labels). The FN-DSA halves in fndsa_signatures are randomized; every other field is a pure function of the two source files. 'expected' is the first refusal of a strict verifier evaluating in the normative order of schema section 7.0: challenge decode D1 to D6, signature serialization I2, then V1 to V6.
